# Model cards

**SIMULATED DATA.** One card per deployed model. Generated by `ml/report_ml.py` from the saved metrics. Every model here was trained and evaluated on simulated data only; none is validated for use in a real mill.

## Noise forecaster (`models/forecast_noise_dba_{30,60}.pkl`)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Forecast zone NOISE 30 and 60 min ahead for the Live Zones view and early warning. |
| **Inputs** | 60 zone features at t (`ml/features.py`): lags, rolling statistics, rate of change, temperature/RH/CO2, machine state, occupancy, time of day, shift, break, zone. |
| **Label source** | Measured zone dBA at t+h (`measured_environmental`). |
| **Output label** | `predicted_risk` (an ML output, per the project's labelling rule). It is a forecast of a zone hazard level, not of anyone's health. |
| **Training window / split** | train: 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z; validation: 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z; test: 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z |
| **Model and hyperparameters** | Chosen per horizon by validation MAE (t+30: random_forest, t+60: random_forest). RF {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_depth': 14, 'min_samples_leaf': 5, 'n_jobs': -1}; XGBoost {'n_estimators': 400, 'max_depth': 6, 'learning_rate': 0.05, 'subsample': 0.8, 'colsample_bytree': 0.8, 'n_jobs': -1}, early stopping 30. Fixed in config.yaml, not grid-searched; seed 42. |
| **Test-day metrics** | t+30: skill +0.805, MAE 1.57 dBA (seasonal baseline +0.765); t+60: skill +0.741, MAE 2.11 dBA (seasonal baseline +0.766) |
| **Known failure modes** | Most skill comes from the fixed timetable; on steady rows skill is lower. At t+60 it does not beat the seasonal baseline. Will degrade when breaks or machine stops are unscheduled. |
| **Intended use** | Zone-level trend and early warning on the dashboard, always beside the measured value. |
| **Must NOT be used for** | Any statement about an individual's health; compliance decisions (it is not a measurement); replacing a sound-level meter or gravimetric sampler. |

## PM2.5 forecaster (`models/forecast_pm25_ugm3_{30,60}.pkl`)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Forecast zone PM2.5 30 and 60 min ahead for the Live Zones view and early warning. |
| **Inputs** | 60 zone features at t (`ml/features.py`): lags, rolling statistics, rate of change, temperature/RH/CO2, machine state, occupancy, time of day, shift, break, zone. |
| **Label source** | Measured zone µg/m³ at t+h (`measured_environmental`). |
| **Output label** | `predicted_risk` (an ML output, per the project's labelling rule). It is a forecast of a zone hazard level, not of anyone's health. |
| **Training window / split** | train: 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z; validation: 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z; test: 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z |
| **Model and hyperparameters** | Chosen per horizon by validation MAE (t+30: xgboost, t+60: xgboost). RF {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_depth': 14, 'min_samples_leaf': 5, 'n_jobs': -1}; XGBoost {'n_estimators': 400, 'max_depth': 6, 'learning_rate': 0.05, 'subsample': 0.8, 'colsample_bytree': 0.8, 'n_jobs': -1}, early stopping 30. Fixed in config.yaml, not grid-searched; seed 42. |
| **Test-day metrics** | t+30: skill +0.384, MAE 38.80 µg/m³ (seasonal baseline +0.254); t+60: skill +0.434, MAE 37.89 µg/m³ (seasonal baseline +0.298) |
| **Known failure modes** | Blowdown and cleaning spikes are only partly predictable; MAE is large in the dustiest zones. Predicts an optical-sensor signal, not a gravimetric concentration. |
| **Intended use** | Zone-level trend and early warning on the dashboard, always beside the measured value. |
| **Must NOT be used for** | Any statement about an individual's health; compliance decisions (it is not a measurement); replacing a sound-level meter or gravimetric sampler. |

| **Inputs** | 60 zone features at t (`ml/features.py`): lags, rolling statistics, rate of change, temperature/RH/CO2, machine state, occupancy, time of day, shift, break, zone. |
| **Label source** | Measured zone °C at t+h (`measured_environmental`). |

RF {'n_estimators': 200, 'max_depth': 14, 'min_samples_leaf': 5, 'n_jobs': -1}; XGBoost {'n_estimators': 400, 'max_depth': 6, 'learning_rate': 0.05, 'subsample': 0.8, 'colsample_bytree': 0.8, 'n_jobs': -1}, early stopping 30. ## Exceedance classifier, `above` (`models/classify_above_h{30,60}.pkl`)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Warn that noise at t+h ≥ 90 dBA. |
| **Inputs** | The same 60 features as the forecasters. |
| **Label source** | Measured noise at t+h vs the india criterion (90 dBA). A future measurement, not a rule on the inputs, so not circular. |
| **Output label** | `predicted_risk` (an ML output). A zone-level hazard flag, not a health estimate. |
| **Training window / split** | train: 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z; validation: 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z; test: 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z |
| **Hyperparameters and search grid** | Grid (validation PR-AUC): `{"logistic_regression": {"C": [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0], "class_weight": [null, "balanced"]}, "random_forest": {"n_estimators": [200], "max_depth": [8, 14, null], "min_samples_leaf": [5, 20]}, "xgboost": {"n_estimators": [400], "max_depth": [3, 6], "learning_rate": [0.05, 0.1], "subsample": [0.8], "colsample_bytree": [0.8]}}`. Chosen: t+30: xgboost {"n_estimators": 400, "max_depth": 6, "learning_rate": 0.1, "subsample": 0.8, "colsample_bytree": 0.8, "best_iteration": 227}, threshold 0.228; t+60: xgboost {"n_estimators": 400, "max_depth": 6, "learning_rate": 0.1, "subsample": 0.8, "colsample_bytree": 0.8, "best_iteration": 178}, threshold 0.248. Threshold: highest validation recall with FPR ≤ 10%. |
| **Test-day metrics** | t+30 (xgboost): prevalence 39.8%, PR-AUC 0.969 (persistence 0.674), F1 0.891, recall 0.926, FPR 0.100; t+60 (xgboost): prevalence 40.1%, PR-AUC 0.968 (persistence 0.673), F1 0.891, recall 0.924, FPR 0.100 |
| **Known failure modes** | High accuracy is mostly base rate in always-loud zones (Z1, Z4, Z5); read PR-AUC and prevalence. |
| **Intended use** | A zone-level early-warning flag for supervisors, shown with its precision (roughly one false alarm per two true ones on `crossing`). |
| **Must NOT be used for** | Reducing any worker's calculated dose; judging compliance; any health statement about a person; replacing measured exceedance alerts. |

## Exceedance classifier, `crossing` (`models/classify_crossing_h{30,60}.pkl`)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Warn that noise below 90 dBA now and ≥ 90 dBA at t+h (a quiet zone about to become hazardous). |
| **Inputs** | The same 60 features as the forecasters. |
| **Label source** | Measured noise at t+h vs the india criterion (90 dBA). A future measurement, not a rule on the inputs, so not circular. |
| **Output label** | `predicted_risk` (an ML output). A zone-level hazard flag, not a health estimate. |
| **Training window / split** | train: 2026-10-20T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z; validation: 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z; test: 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z -> 2026-10-27T00:00:00Z |
| **Hyperparameters and search grid** | Grid (validation PR-AUC): `{"logistic_regression": {"C": [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0], "class_weight": [null, "balanced"]}, "random_forest": {"n_estimators": [200], "max_depth": [8, 14, null], "min_samples_leaf": [5, 20]}, "xgboost": {"n_estimators": [400], "max_depth": [3, 6], "learning_rate": [0.05, 0.1], "subsample": [0.8], "colsample_bytree": [0.8]}}`. Chosen: t+30: xgboost {"n_estimators": 400, "max_depth": 3, "learning_rate": 0.05, "subsample": 0.8, "colsample_bytree": 0.8, "best_iteration": 193}, threshold 0.192; t+60: xgboost {"n_estimators": 400, "max_depth": 6, "learning_rate": 0.05, "subsample": 0.8, "colsample_bytree": 0.8, "best_iteration": 160}, threshold 0.181. Threshold: highest validation recall with FPR ≤ 10%. |
| **Test-day metrics** | t+30 (xgboost): prevalence 15.9%, PR-AUC 0.834 (persistence 0.159), F1 0.683, recall 0.776, FPR 0.094; t+60 (xgboost): prevalence 16.2%, PR-AUC 0.841 (persistence 0.162), F1 0.680, recall 0.807, FPR 0.110 |
| **Known failure modes** | The pooled PR-AUC is driven by trivial restarts in always-loud zones and the office's certain negatives. In the borderline zones (Z2, Z3, Z6), where a warning matters, PR-AUC is about twice chance; in Z2 (carding, at the criterion) it barely beats chance, and one pooled threshold gives Z2 a false-alarm rate of 44–53%. Do not deploy as a Z2 warning without zone-specific thresholds and better features. |
| **Intended use** | A zone-level early-warning flag for supervisors, shown with its precision (roughly one false alarm per two true ones on `crossing`). |
| **Must NOT be used for** | Reducing any worker's calculated dose; judging compliance; any health statement about a person; replacing measured exceedance alerts. |

## Machine condition monitor — EWMA control chart (`ml/anomaly.py`, deployed detector)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Flag a machine whose vibration has drifted from its own baseline (wear). |
| **Inputs** | 10-min mean vib_rms_g of running-only, unflagged readings. |
| **Label source** | None for training (unsupervised). Scored against `machines[].degrading` in config.yaml. |
| **Training window** | Each machine's own first 1 day (Phase I reference). |
| **Parameters** | λ = 0.1, limits ±3.5σ (exact width), alarm = 3 consecutive flagged bins. Set before results were seen. |
| **Metrics** | M5 detected on day 2.08; healthy machines alarmed: none; healthy per-bin FPR 0.02%. |
| **Known failure modes** | Calibrating on a day when the machine is already wearing inflates its baseline and delays detection. Mean-only, so it misses faults that change crest factor without moving RMS. Tested only on one smooth simulated wear curve. |
| **Intended use** | A maintenance prompt to inspect the machine. |
| **Must NOT be used for** | Fault diagnosis (it says *that* vibration changed, not *why*); claims about worker health; shutting a machine down without inspection. |

## Machine condition monitor — isolation forest (compared, not deployed)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Unsupervised comparison for the EWMA chart. |
| **Inputs** | RMS, peak, crest factor, 1-h rolling means of RMS and peak. |
| **Parameters** | 200 trees, seed 42; flag above the 99% quantile of reference scores. |
| **Metrics** | Detected on day 2.12; healthy per-bin FPR 1.03%. |
| **Why not deployed** | No earlier detection than the control chart, a ~50× higher per-bin false-positive rate, and harder for a maintenance engineer to interpret. |

## Risk index (`exposure/risk_index.py`) — listed for completeness; NOT a trained model

| | |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | Order worker-days by exposure for review. |
| **Label** | `deterministic_index`: a formula, no training and no labels. |
| **Reported with** | The worst single component beside the weighted composite (components are not on commensurable scales), and both noise doses. |
| **Must NOT be used for** | Diagnosis of any condition; estimating the probability of a health outcome. The ML risk classifier is deferred until questionnaire or audiometry labels exist. |
